name: held-out example
wording: An example the architect writes or has written cold and holds back from the build when a story's risk warrants, kept with the design apart from the visible examples. It is used only in review: whoever reviews the story's changes, an agent or the operator, takes it from there directly, so nothing about it passes through whoever runs the build, and a story whose changes ship has none. It is held back by omission alone, never named in a task or mentioned to a builder, since a prohibition would announce it. When one fails, builders learn its concept and the general rule of the failed clause, never the case or a prescribed change; the exposed case becomes visible and the illustrator writes a cold replacement for the next review.
reason: The operator: the design state a session reads was long human prose restating facts across concepts and carrying decisions with their situations; its reader is a model, so the state is the design alone, each concept as its established name and residue, and decisions and their reasons are history. Restated as its established name and residue, standalone, each fact in the one concept it belongs to, with the meaning standing decisions carried folded in.
